correctness.rationale: Independent rate-one clocks have independent Exp(1) first arrivals and an almost surely unique last first arrival. Conditional on its time t and index, the other counts are independent Poisson(t) conditioned positive; the last type contributes one singleton. Thus S_n | W_n=t has law 1+Bin(n−1,t/(e^t−1)). At t=log n+g the conditional mean is (log n)e^(−g)+O(1) and the conditional variance divided by log n tends to e^(−g), uniformly for g in a compact set. Expanding the centered binomial characteristic function, using tightness of W_n−log n and the explicit maximum distribution, gives the claimed joint mixed-Gaussian law. The variance of W_n−T_n/n is H_n/n from the label-independent Exp(n) gaps, so even (log n)|W_n−T_n/n| tends to zero in probability, and replacing the center preserves the Gaussian scale. Division by e^(−X_n/2) gives the independent standard normal pivot. For the covariance, under the singleton weighting S_n−1 the substitution u=e^(−W_n) yields Beta(2,n−1) integrals for −log u and its square; these give E[S_n]=H_n and Cov(W_n,S_n)=H_n^(2)−H_n. With Beta(3,n−2) one obtains the stated second factorial moment; the resulting Var(S_n)∼(log n)² gives the correlation limit. A separate exact rational recurrence reproduces Cov(T_n,S_n)=−1/2, −17/12, −95/36 for n=2,3,4, respectively (branches/306200d7-af4a-4194-94c4-09791336ff4d/independent_finite_check.py); these checks are finite, not a proof of the limit. Frozen verification support was inspected, not executed.

value.rationale: A Gaussian pivot independent of the completion fluctuation is useful in the coupon model, but this submission's pivot is a coordinate of an existing broader theorem, changed by a routine recentering and continuous reparametrization.
